searchDocs.title: draw​
searchDocs.content: </> RayLens.draw( origin: Vector3 ,-- Where the ray started direction: Vector3 ,-- The vector you cast, its length is the ray length result: RaycastResult?,-- The cast result or nil for a miss options: Options?-- Styling, blank fields fall back to the defaults ) → () Draws an already casted ray, show the result you got from worldRoot:Raycast, a nil result is nothing, drawn at full length with no marker, so the absent marker is what tells you it missed, a result is drawn to its hit point with a marker on the surface normal

searchDocs.title: ray​
searchDocs.content: </> RayLens.ray( origin: Vector3 ,-- Where the ray started direction: Vector3 ,-- Direction and length options: Options?-- Styling, blank fields just go to the defaults ) → () Draws a ray before or without casting it, direction carries its own length, matches worldRoot:Raycast(o, d), so the same vector can be passed to both

searchDocs.content: </> RayLens.clear() → () Removes every drawn adornment and stops the loop

searchDocs.title: onDraw​
searchDocs.content: </> RayLens.onDraw( callback: DrawCallback?-- Called once per frame with the frame delta, or nil to stop ) → () Adds a per frame callback, while the one that's set the previous frame is cleared before each call, so it draws inside the callback to create a new picture every frame and never rely on a lifetime, show nil to stop
